Item 0, follow-ups from /home/alfakentavr/scribe/docs/build/08-codex-review-batch-a.md (read its "New defects" and "V1 supervisor" sections):
- P2 state lock: `pre_tool_use_gate.plan_verdict` (and any other caller that reads state through an `update_state` mutation callback) must read pending decisions from the returned state, so a lock timeout never turns into a false deny; test: hold `state.json.lock` past the timeout, submit a plan in enforce mode with pending decisions present, expect allow.
- P2 rm rule: `policy` must keep command boundaries (newline, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`) before scanning rm flags and targets; test the negative case `rm build` newline `printf '%s\n' -rf /tmp/example` (must not match) and keep the positive `rm -rf build /tmp/other`.
- V1 marker provenance: the supervisor generates a random per-invocation token, passes it to the child in the environment variable `SCRIBE_DENY_TOKEN`, and `scribe.protocol.announce_deny` prints `[scribe-deny <token>]`; the supervisor accepts only that exact line, so a traceback containing `[scribe-deny]` can no longer impersonate a denial. When the marker is validated, the supervisor forces the blocking status itself: exit 2 for `hook` invocations, exit 1 for `git-hook` invocations, whatever the child returned. Add `-S` next to `-I` in hooks/hooks.json and in the timing and supervisor tests. The git shim re-executes itself under `sys.executable -I -S` when `sys.flags.isolated` is false (wrapped in try, fail open). Update README's fail-open bullet and the hooks.json test accordingly. Tests: traceback impersonation is mapped to exit 0; marker plus exit 0 from the child still yields exit 2 for a hook and 1 for a git hook; the shim re-exec path.

Item 1, V12 "attested, live, not superseded". One shared predicate, for example `store.effective_authority(record)` returning True only when: the latest attestation for the record is `ratified` with `body_sha256` equal to the current body hash; `effective_state` is `proposed` or `implemented`; and no effective supersession edge points at the record. The Bash and PowerShell gate (`pre_tool_use_gate.action_is_ratified` or its successor) uses it; INDEX.md's active list and commit-msg's active_records reuse it where they currently re-derive the same idea. Fix the test helper `write_ratified_action_record` so it writes a real attestation, and add negative tests: unattested, expired, superseded, body hash mismatch. Also: after an enforce-mode denial, TaskCompleted must NOT clear `decision_worthy` (the retry needs a record first); shadow mode keeps today's behaviour. Test both.

Item 2, V3 "refuse dirty ledger, base tip". `scribe check --base <ref>` exits 1 with a clear message when `git status --porcelain -- docs/decisions` is non-empty, unless `--allow-dirty` is given; the predecessor-was-ratified question is answered against the base ref's tip (the ref as given), not the merge base, while changed paths and commits still come from the merge base range. Tests: dirty ledger refused and allowed; a ratification added on the target branch after the fork is honoured. Document the flag in README's CLI table and in the scribe-check.yml template only if CI needs it (it should not: CI checkouts are clean).

Item 3, V8 "one ledger lock everywhere". New record files are created with exclusive create (`open(path, "x")` or `O_EXCL`) so two `scribe new` runs with the same title cannot overwrite each other (the loser picks the next `-2` suffix or fails cleanly, say which in an I-line). The existing ratify lock (`state.locked` or its successor from V9) is also taken by `scribe new --register`, post-commit, relink and `lint --expire`, and every one of them reloads the records after acquiring the lock. On lock timeout each of them behaves like V9's ratify: one stderr line, no ledger write, non-zero exit for CLI commands, exit 0 for the git hook (fail open, nothing written). Tests: alias race with a pre-created file, lock held past the timeout for each writer.

Item 4, V19 "no cap, prune on expiry". Remove the 20-entry cap on `pending_decisions`; ids stay until a commit consumes them or the session is pruned by the existing expiry. Update the plan reference in the code comment and any test that asserted the cap.

Item 5, V21 "subdirectory start". Live tests showed that NO project settings (`.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json`, relative, `**` or absolute rules) load when Claude Code starts in a subdirectory of the repo, so the deny rule only protects sessions started at the repo root. Implement: (a) the SessionStart hook compares the payload `cwd` with the repository root and, when they differ, prints one line of additionalContext such as `scribe: session started below the repository root; the RATIFICATIONS.jsonl deny rule from .claude/settings.json is not active here; start Claude at <root> or add Edit(**/docs/decisions/RATIFICATIONS.jsonl) to your user settings` (advisory, exit 0); (b) `scribe init` prints a similar hint in its next-steps block; (c) README's ratification section states the limitation and the user-level rule. Tests for (a) and (b). Do not write user settings.
